title: stream chunk reassembly + function-call sentinel guards to avoid partial-JSON emission
author: Diego Chen
description: Context: The OpenAI-compat SSE shim occasionally emitted events that left receiver-side JSON parsers with partial/unterminated objects when downstream tokenization caused chunk boundaries to cut inside structured fields (function_call, choices[].delta, or metadata objects). This surfaced as truncated function_call payloads and out-of-order 'content' fragments in a small subset of integration tests and customer reports. Motivation: Make the shim robust to chunking/race cases and ensure we never send an SSE data: line that contains an incomplete JSON object for tokens that are expected to be reassembled by the client. Summary of changes: 1) Reassembly buffer with explicit sentinel markers: add a lightweight per-stream reassembly buffer that delays emitting an SSE "data:" line until either a sentinel sequence is observed (closing brace for small objects, OpenAI-style [DONE], or explicit function_call boundary marker) or the buffer reaches a safe flush size. 2) Function-call sentinel handling: when the model starts emitting a function_call object, the shim now tracks a mini-state machine (start, in_object, escaped, complete) keyed by the top-level field name. This prevents flushing a partial function_call delta, which previously produced invalid JSON for clients expecting a single object. 3) Deterministic chunk coalescing policy: replace time-based heuristics with hybrid size/time windows (8KB OR 25ms, whichever comes first) to reduce micro-reordering on busy connections while keeping latency SLOs for small responses. 4) Delimiter de-duplication and trimming: ensure we dedupe duplicated newline delimiters introduced by upstream tokenizers and normalize event separators to a single '\n' to avoid empty events. 5) Tests & logging: add end-to-end SSE harness tests for (a) truncated-brace scenarios, (b) interleaved choices[].delta streams, and (c) function_call stream completion. New debug logs are guarded behind debug flags to avoid noise in production. Backwards compatibility: behavior is compatible with existing clients; only difference is that very small intermediate fragments may be delayed up to 25ms (configurable) to guarantee atomicity of structured fields. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind COMPAT_SSE_REASSEMBLY; start with canary for internal customers and opt-in beta for select enterprise tenants. If instrumentation shows no regressions after 48h, flip for all users. Tests: unit tests for buffer state machine, fuzz tests for random chunk boundaries, integration tests simulating half-sent syntactic tokens. Performance: CPU overhead measured ~+0.7% on synthetic load; median latency for 95th percentile responses increased by <= 6ms due to coalescing window on small responses. Risk & mitigations: risk of added latency for small single-token responses; mitigated by allowing per-tenant overrides and per-route configuration. Related: partially addresses SUP-4921 (customer seeing malformed function_call JSON) and ENG-2147 (SSE event atomicity). Checklist: - [x] Reassembly state machine implemented - [x] Unit + fuzz tests added - [x] Integration tests added against reference SSE client - [x] Canary rollout plan documented - [x] Review feedback addressed.

review_comments: Ava Martinez: Nice isolation of the state machine. One question: how does this interact with existing prefix/KV caching? Could cached prefixes be flushed before we see the sentinel?

Diego Chen: The reassembly buffer operates after prefix cache application. We only buffer emitted SSE data after cache has been applied so behavioral semantics are preserved. Added comment in code and unit test to assert ordering.
Priya Kapoor: Can we make the coalesce window configurable per-route? Some latency-sensitive endpoints shouldn't wait 25ms.
Diego Chen: Added per-route override and tenant-level flag; default remains 25ms but can be set to 0ms to preserve previous behavior.

release_notes: Fixes cases where SSE streaming emitted partial/invalid JSON for structured fields (function_call, choices[].delta). Introduces an opt-in reassembly buffer and deterministic chunk coalescing to ensure atomic delivery of structured events. Backwards-compatible but may add configurable micro-coalescing latency on small responses.
